directions.a:
Create a production environment concept sheet for a room update, not a prop catalog or a finished game screenshot. Use TWO LANDSCAPE PANELS STACKED VERTICALLY, with a thin neutral divider and no title or annotation inside the image. Top panel matches reference image 1's camera looking toward the DJ window; bottom panel matches reference image 2's opposing camera toward the rear storage/listening wall. Both panels must describe exactly the SAME room, furniture inventory and arrangement.

REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 and image 2 are current native rendered views and locked architectural/perspective guides, not style targets. Preserve their actual floor size, tall concrete ceiling, large rounded-corner window and its mullions, every existing doorway, external city scale and perspective, ducts, conduits, electrical boxes and approved magenta LCS gas-neon sign. Do not invent an opening, change walls, lower the ceiling, enlarge the window, stretch the room or enlarge the rugs. Retain the existing analog two-turntable DJ station beside the window as the main work focus. Remove the character from these environmental studies.

DIRECTION A — SOCIAL BROADCAST DEN: Vibe collected and repaired this furniture herself. Make the room visibly more occupied, busy, intimate and personal with substantial furniture masses. Keep the existing tobacco sofa as the listening anchor and existing ochre armchair. Add a substantial low salvaged wooden coffee table within reach of the sofa, a second mismatched worn lounge chair angled into this conversation group, and a long low record credenza assembled from mismatched rescued timber cabinets along suitable solid wall. Integrate the existing steel shelves as visibly stocked storage behind this domestic sitting space. Retain an open connected route from the doors to the DJ operating position.

Give all added furniture believable physical weight and varied heights. Use one small battered side surface beside a chair, a couple of heavy crates in lower cabinet/shelf pockets and a supported soft throw plus two mismatched cushions. Clutter forms use-specific clusters: open record sleeves and a partly selected stack on the coffee table, magazines, a notebook with loose papers and pencil, one or two coffee mugs away from audio controls, headphones resting on a safe edge, irregular records/books/boxed tapes on shelves. Leave useful gaps and accessible handles. Loosen the current uniform poster row into a few overlapping personal wall groups above seating/credenza, combining the approved fictional poster imagery already visible in the references with pinned small notes and photographs; art reads as actual printed artwork, not presentation cards or color swatches.

PLACEMENT CONCEPT: Furniture occupies feasible listening, media-storage and broadcast-support zones; contents rest on compatible real carrying surfaces. Heavy crates low, flat sleeves/papers on tables, books/tapes on shelves, textiles on seating. Nothing floating, leaning through another object, pasted on controls or blocking electrical service access. Keep doors and circulation usable. No arbitrarily scattered objects across bare floor. Show a genuinely busy mid-ground, not only extra tiny shelf props.

LOOK: Photorealistic environment concept art with clear readable shapes and ordinary warm incandescent evening light from the existing practical fixtures, cool grey city light through the existing window. Worn tobacco/ochre fabric, mixed aged woods, patched muted upholstery, scuffed steel. Lived-in and cared for, rescued from different places; no boutique interior, matched furniture suite or showroom styling. Avoid using exaggerated bloom or darkness as a substitute for density. No plants, perishables, real brands, fresh food, candles, LCD/LED screens, RGB strips, extra neon, second DJ deck, invented large signage or new canon slogans. Same furniture and grouped clutter in both opposing panels.
directions.b:
Create a production environment concept sheet for an update of Vienna/Vibe's main room. TWO LANDSCAPE PANELS STACKED VERTICALLY, separated by one thin neutral line, no title or annotation inside the image. Top panel uses exactly reference image1's camera toward the main DJ window; bottom panel uses exactly reference image2's opposing camera toward the rear storage/listening wall. Same coherent room, same furniture inventory and physical arrangement in both panels.

REFERENCE ROLES: The two images are current native room views and authoritative architectural/camera guides. Lock the real room footprint, tall ceiling, actual large rounded window and mullions, external city scale and perspective, existing doorways, concrete walls/floor, ducts, conduits and electrical service cabinets. Preserve the existing approved magenta LCS gas-neon sign. Do not invent an opening, extend a wall, enlarge the window or rugs, stretch perspective or change room proportions. Remove the moving character for a clear environment study. Retain the existing analog DJ station with its two turntables beside the window, the tobacco sofa and the ochre armchair as the same objects. No second DJ setup.

DIRECTION B — WORKING RECORD ARCHIVE: This is a busy home broadcasting room that Vibe stocked by bringing furniture from different places. Add several substantial mixed-height furniture masses, giving the currently vacant mid-ground a real function. Add a waist-high worn wooden record browsing cabinet with open bins of upright records, a narrow salvaged sorting table and a mismatched worn office chair, and a small loaded steel utility trolley within the broadcast-support area. Build an irregular storage wall from one tall rescued timber bookcase, mismatched closed lower cabinets and the existing metal shelving. The sofa remains a comfortable secondary listening/rest corner with a rumpled supported throw and cushion. This direction is distinct from a lounge: prominent record browsing and sorting surfaces, more storage volume, busier active collection.

Clutter is concentrated in useful groups: an open record sleeve beside a selected stack on the sorting table, paper divider cards and a handwritten selection notebook, labelled cassette cartons and books on lower shelves, a current batch of records and tape boxes on the trolley, spare sleeves in supported trays, a coiled wired headphone lead beside safe audio gear, a coffee mug on a clear side surface. Show uneven filled and empty shelf pockets, crooked rows of record spines and several boxes with plain taped labels. Do not add piles of random floor rubbish. Make a dense working noticeboard near the sorting surface, with small notes, approved character photographs and tickets, and a few overlapping existing fictional posters around it, instead of repeating a uniform poster stripe. Poster art remains pictorial finished printed art rather than UI cards.

PLACEMENT FEASIBILITY: Furniture belongs to listening, media-storage and broadcast-support zones, uses real free floor/wall pockets and keeps connected human-width routes from the doors to all stations. Heavy crates and dense media bins on load-bearing lower shelves; small books/tapes/record piles on compatible shelves or tables; notes on clear wall/board patches; textiles on seats. Doors, electrical cabinets, turntable controls, speakers, microphone and the operator's space remain accessible. No floating or intersecting items. Never use an arbitrary camera-only pose. Preserve readable clear desk pockets among the clutter.

LOOK: Photorealistic environment concept art, believable readable material and shape, warm ordinary existing incandescent fixtures against cool grey overcast city light. Collected aged brown timber, rescued muted steel, faded olive/plum/brown fabric, paper wear, quiet repaired joints. Personal and cared for but makeshift; no boutique design, uniform matching modular furniture, retail record shop signage, professional showroom or fabricated technical UI. Do not disguise emptiness with huge bloom, darkness or visual effects. No plants, perishables, fresh food, candles, real brands, LCD/LED screens, RGB strips, extra neon, new canon text, changed kitchen or added doorways. Exactly the same added furniture and clutter groups across both opposing views.
